hypothesis: a one-bar rail escape followed by completed-bar re-entry is a stop-hunt-like failed auction; requiring prior boundary crowding, abnormal completed-bar energy, opposite response, and spread relaxation selects reversals with more raw movement per decision

causal_chronology.history: 24 completed M5 bars ending before event bar i
causal_chronology.event: completed M5 bar i crosses exactly one 24-bar rail
causal_chronology.response: completed M5 bar i+1 must remain inside the prior rail and close opposite the escape
causal_chronology.fill: next recorded executable BID/ASK open at i+2
causal_chronology.exit: fixed close of i+26, equal to 24 M5 bars after fill

original_indicator.name: Auction Trap Geometry
fixed_structural_gate: at least 2 of the previous 24 bars touched the escaped rail within 0.25 causal scale
event squared close-return energy is at least the median squared close-return energy of the previous 23 returns
escape distance is at least 0.10 causal scale
response close remains at least 0.10 causal scale inside the rail
response close-to-close return is opposite the escape
response closing spread is no wider than event closing spread

cost_arms.RAW_SIGNAL: mid-open to mid-close exact directional ratio; zero execution cost
cost_arms.EXECUTABLE_BASE: observed BID/ASK plus 0.3 pip one-way slippage and 0.5 bps/day financing
cost_arms.ADVERSE_STRESS: observed BID/ASK plus 0.9 pip one-way slippage, 0.2 bps one-way commission, and 1.5 bps/day financing

development_admission: walk-forward RAW_SIGNAL mean return is positive
walk-forward EXECUTABLE_BASE mean return is positive
walk-forward ADVERSE_STRESS mean return is positive
final_admission: not available from opened development data; requires untouched full comparable months with normal and adverse equity at least 2.0x
